rationale: A is better structured, broader, and more actionable, with a stronger emphasis on targeted long-span detection rather than generic token penalties that can damage legitimate reasoning. Its ranking appropriately prioritizes decode-time span matching and serving-side containment for verbatim loops, while clearly separating immediate mitigations from weight-level fixes. It also gives more useful implementation details and generally better-calibrated caveats. Some claims are overstated—especially that DPO pairs are effectively free, that progress markers make looping impossible, and that the decoder change is only a few lines—but B has more consequential technical weaknesses, including implying that a diverse speculative proposer changes exact speculative-decoding behavior, claiming ordered-step grammars prevent cycling, and asserting that streaming detection catches every loop.
